subject: SCCs path & evidence plan for QH Healthcare integration
messages:
From: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@qh-health.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.example>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>
Cc: Elena Vos <elena.vos@qhcounsel.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Aug 2026 09:07:00 +0100
Subject: Guidance request — transfer clause and evidence for upcoming integration

Hi Logan / Marissa / Neha,

Thanks for taking this on. We are moving forward with a production integration between QH Healthcare (controller) and Redwood (processor) and our legal team has asked for: 1) confirmation on which SCC module we should execute for EU and UK residents, and 2) a checklist of the operational evidence your team can provide (SOC 2 summary, subprocessors list, DPIA touches).

Quick context: the integration will process patient identifiers and treatment summaries (pseudonymised where possible). Primary processing will occur in Frankfurt with a small subset routed to a UK analytics partner for model evaluation. Our counsel (Elena) is on copy — they prefer a recommended path + minimal exceptions so our procurement can sign off this week if possible.

Can you confirm:
- Which SCC module(s) you recommend for EU -> Redwood (controller -> processor) and any separate step for the UK transfer?
- Typical evidence you can hand over within 48-72 hours to satisfy procurement (SOC 2 scope, subprocessors, DPA redline pointers)?
- Any known blockers (e.g., subprocessors that trigger additional approvals)?

Appreciate a short, actionable reply — we’re trying to lock the MSA this week.

Best,
Rajiv
Head of Integrations, QH Healthcare

---

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.example>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.example>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.example>, Elena Vos <elena.vos@qhcounsel.com>

Subject: Re: Guidance request — transfer clause and evidence for upcoming integration

Rajiv / Elena — thanks for the context. High level recommendation + next steps below so procurement has something concise to work with: 

Recommendation (short):
- Primary route: Controller -> Processor SCC path (Controller-to-Processor module) for EU data; we recommend executing the SCC Module that maps to a controller->processor relationship as Redwoods’ standard DPA attachment.
- UK handling: Add the UK-compatible addendum and mirror the same clauses; where UK-only routing to a third party occurs, include a targeted UK-specific clause to cover onward transfers (we can supply language).

Why this path: it preserves a clear controller/processor boundary for both EU and UK and keeps scope limited to the standard DPA flow that procurement expects. It avoids a processor-to-processor module election which would require additional contractual flow-downs to your analytics partner.

Evidence we can provide quickly (48–72h):
- Redwood SOC 2 summary (scope: security + availability) — we can provide the auditor’s cover page and controls map.
- Current subprocessors list + processing location table (including country + purpose).
- Redacted data flow map for the integration and a short DPIA comment on residual re-identification risk.
- Standard DPA + suggested SCC language (PDF) and a DocuSign-ready packet.

Potential blockers to flag:
- If your UK analytics partner requires independent DPA terms (they may want to be a joint controller for analytics outputs), that could shift the module choice — please confirm their role.
- Any requirement for full patient-level export to non-EU/UK jurisdictions will trigger additional safeguards (we can advise but will need time).

Proposed short timeline:
- Today: we attach checklist + SOC 2 summary (see attached).
- Tomorrow: your counsel reviews suggested SCC attachments; we iterate on any small redlines.
- Fri EOD: target execution-ready DocuSign packet if there are no material redlines.

Attachments: QH-SCCs-Evidence-Checklist.xlsx, redwood-sccs-selection-rationale.pdf, redwood-soc2-summary.pdf

If useful, I can set a 30-minute call with Marissa (legal) and Neha (privacy) to walk counsel through the rationale — let me know times that work.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Senior Sales Lead — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Logan — this is helpful, thanks. Two quick clarifications: 
1) Our UK partner is acting strictly as a subprocesser for model evaluation; they won’t receive identifiers, only hashed tokens. Does that materially change the recommendation?
2) Procurement asked specifically whether the SOC 2 summary will include cover for change control and release management (they want assurance around model updates).

We’re available for a 30-minute slot tomorrow afternoon UK time if Marissa / Neha can join. Also please confirm whether redwood’s subprocessors list includes any third-country subprocessors that would complicate the DocuSign package.

Rajiv

Rajiv / Elena — quick follow-up after internal sync with Legal & Privacy. Summary and actionables below.

Short answers: 
- UK subprocessors receiving hashed tokens: we still recommend preserving the controller->processor SCC path for primary contract. Because only tokenized outputs go to the UK partner, this reduces the need for processor-to-processor routing, but we will include a narrow onward-transfer clause in the UK addendum to reflect that flow.
- SOC 2 scope: our SOC 2 summary includes change control and release management controls (CC5 / change control mappings). I attached the SOC 2 summary page; the full report can be shared under NDA.

What I attached in this message (attached files):
- QH-SCCs-Evidence-Checklist.xlsx — checklist broken into DPA, SCCs, SOC2 items, subprocessors, DPIA notes
- redwood-sccs-selection-rationale.pdf — 1-page rationale you can paste into your procurement memo
- redwood-soc2-summary.pdf — auditor cover + scope snapshot

Next steps (proposed):
1) Elena / QH counsel: review the rationale PDF and the checklist and highlight any redlines you expect in the SCC annex.
2) If minor: we produce a DocuSign-ready packet (link below) and target execution this week.
3) If material: schedule a 30-min call Monday with Marissa & Neha to resolve specifics.

DocuSign packet (pre-populated): https://app.redwood.example/docusign/qh-sccs-12345
Data flow sketch (internal): https://sharedrive.company/controls/qh-data-mapping-v2

If you want me to loop in Ops for a live walkthrough of subprocessors and the model deployment lifecycle, tell me a time and I’ll book it.

Cheers,
Logan Wright
